Sixteen comments

L’Air Mignonne

This is a tune composed by Simon Riopel from Montreal. He plays it in alternate tuning as AEAE.

Here’s a youtube of Simon playing it:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pGaiiCRJg7U

I learned this tune from Yan Falquet in June, 2014 while he was visiting at a fiddle camp in California. He played it on his concertina, and it has a really nice French air feel to it.

↳ Posted by JoJofidhlear on January 11th, 2015.

L’Air Mignonne

I forgot to add that the title means “cute, little tune.” And it is that.

Re: L’Air Mignonne

Just edited the abc’s for this tune. It was my first learn-by-ear tune and then I transcribed it to abc format. Just came back to it, and realized it needed some help. Nice to know I have made a wee bit of progress since my first endeavors.

↳ Posted by JoJofidhlear on August 25th, 2016.

Fancy title ?

The French word for “tune” is masculine so it should be “l’air mignon” !
I don’t know Quebec idioms but from France this title really sounds like a wordplay between “the cute tune” and “(the girl who) looks cute” ;-)

↳ Posted by Ulysse on November 26th, 2016.

Re: L’Air Mignonne

Simon Riopel, knowingly or unwittingly must have derived this tune from the 3/4 march or 9/8 slip jig ‘The Eagle’s whistle’ (also known as The Cry of the Women at the Slaughter = Gol na mBan san Ár).
Check the melodic contour there for comparison;
3/4 version: https://thesession.org/tunes/4192
9/8 version: https://thesession.org/tunes/9853
There was even an attempt at a polka take on it here (X:1);
https://thesession.org/tunes/1837 ..although I find the 4/4 offered by Simon more convincing by far.

↳ Posted by birlibirdie on March 8th, 2024.

Re: L’Air Mignonne

The composer of this tune, Simon Riopel, plays a C# as the last note in the 2nd and 6th measures here: https://youtu.be/pGaiiCRJg7U

Many others (on YouTube and posted above, including the Ímar video mentioned above) play it as a B. In G major, those notes would be B and A.

↳ Posted by David Barnert on May 2nd, 2025.
